items.title: Ineba Gogo MFB

caseStudy.role: Website Designer — responsible for the website’s visual design and interface layouts.
caseStudy.problem: Ineba Gogo Microfinance Bank needed a new website where prospective customers could find the business, understand its services, and learn how to open an account. The design needed to introduce the bank clearly and make its personal and business banking offerings easy to explore.
caseStudy.decisions:
I organised the content into distinct sections covering the bank, its services, its values, and its banking products. This gives visitors a clear path from learning about the business to exploring a relevant service.

The interface combines dark backgrounds, lighter content sections, and bright accents to distinguish information and highlight calls to action. Product cards separate personal and business banking, while icons support the service descriptions and values.

On mobile, the content follows a single-column layout with stacked cards and a compact navigation menu.
caseStudy.result: The new website gave people a place to discover the bank, understand what it offers, and find a route to opening an account. It established an online presence that supports both learning about the business and taking the next step towards becoming a customer.

items.title: Belema Fintech Website

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body:
Belema Fintech wanted its existing website to look better and feel more presentable, while showing the full range of its services and products.

My responsibility was the website’s design. The focus was on improving the visual presentation and organising information so visitors could understand the business and explore its offerings.

sections.heading: Giving the content a clear hierarchy
sections.body:
The design uses large headings to establish the main message, followed by supporting copy and smaller groups of information. In the services section, icons and short headings separate the company’s key benefits into distinct points.

Light backgrounds give the content room to breathe, while green accents and a colourful illustration connect the section to the brand. This creates a clear visual order for visitors scanning the page.

images.caption: The services section groups key benefits beneath a prominent heading, with supporting icons and an illustration.
images.alt: Belema Fintech services section with benefit descriptions on the left and a colourful infrastructure illustration on the right.

sections.heading: Introducing the business
sections.body:
The About page pairs a clear statement of what Belema does with a more detailed company introduction. The two-column layout separates the headline from the explanation, keeping each easy to scan.

A company-logo strip sits below the introduction, adding visual context to the business presentation without competing with the main message.

images.caption: The About page combines a bold introduction, supporting company information and a company-logo strip.
images.alt: Belema Fintech About page showing a large headline, company description and logos beneath the introduction.

sections.heading: Making products and contact details easy to find
sections.body:
The main navigation groups the website into familiar destinations: Home, About Us, Products, Resources and Contact Us.

The footer provides another route to the product pages and brings together company information, support links, contact details and office locations. Its dark green background and lime brand mark create a distinct ending to the page.

images.caption: The footer organises product links, company information and contact details into separate columns.
images.alt: Dark green Belema Fintech footer with product links, contact information, office addresses and social links.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.body:
The redesigned website gave Belema Fintech a more polished presentation of its products, services and company information.

I also observed higher search rankings after launch. This is a qualitative observation; the case study does not attribute that improvement to visual design alone.

caseStudy.role: Website Designer — responsible for the visual design and interface layouts.
caseStudy.summary: I redesigned Belema Fintech’s website to give the business a more polished online presence and present its products and services clearly. The design brings together structured content, bold typography and the brand’s green palette to help visitors explore what the company offers.

items.description: A redesign of Belema Fintech’s website, giving its payment products and services a clearer, more professional presentation.

items.title: Food Couriers
items.description: A food-delivery app design bringing meal discovery, product details and order review into a connected mobile experience.

caseStudy.summary: Food Couriers is a client food-delivery app project I designed in Figma. The work explores the journey from browsing meals to reviewing an order, supported by research involving 20 participants. I delivered the completed interface designs to the client.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body:
The project centred on a mobile food-delivery experience. The design needed to bring food discovery, meal information and order review into a connected journey.

My responsibility was the app's UI/UX design. I developed the interface screens and their visual presentation for delivery to the client.

sections.heading: Research and the core journeys
sections.body:
The research phase involved 20 participants. The project presentation also documented task flows for getting started with the app and placing a food order.

These flows frame the experience around two practical tasks: reaching the home screen and moving from selecting a meal to reviewing an order. The final screens show how those tasks connect across the app.

sections.heading: From browsing to choosing a meal
sections.body:
The home screen brings together the delivery location, search, food categories, promotional offers and meal cards. Images, prices and ratings give people information to compare while browsing.

The food-detail screen gives the selected meal more space, pairing a large image with its name, supporting information and a prominent action at the bottom. This creates a visual transition from exploring several options to considering one item.

images.caption: Meal discovery combines search, categories, offers and food cards.
images.alt: Food Couriers home screen with food categories, a promotional banner and meal cards.

images.caption: The detail screen brings the selected meal into focus.
images.alt: Food Couriers meal-detail screen with a large burger photograph and product information.

sections.heading: Reviewing the order and managing a profile
sections.body:
The order screen groups selected meals into separate rows with quantity controls. A summary area beneath the items brings the price breakdown and order action together.

The profile screen separates personal information from contact details and provides an edit action. Both screens use grouped information and clear headings to make their content easier to scan.

images.caption: Order review groups meal selections, quantities and a price summary.
images.alt: Food Couriers order screen showing three food items, quantity controls and an order summary.

images.caption: Profile information is organised into personal and contact sections.
images.alt: Food Couriers profile screen with an avatar, personal information, contact details and an edit button.

sections.heading: A consistent visual language
sections.body:
The interface combines pink and red accents with light backgrounds, rounded cards and food photography. Poppins typography provides a consistent style across headings, labels and supporting text.

Food illustrations and decorative line drawings give the app a recognisable character. Stronger accent colours draw attention to primary actions and selected navigation elements.

sections.heading: Delivery and reflection
sections.body:
I delivered the completed interface designs to the client, covering the welcome experience, meal discovery, food details, order review and profile management.

Looking back, my next iteration would focus on interface-copy consistency, accurate price calculations and task-based usability testing of the ordering flow. These checks would help refine the design before implementation.
